name: cns
description: The Convex Name System: resolve a name such as convex.fungible, register or update one the owner controls, the standard library names. Load for a Convex name, an @name, or which address a library lives at.

content.inline:
# Convex Name System

CNS maps readable names such as `convex.fungible` to addresses, so code and conversation can use names instead of numbers.

## Resolve

- In source, `@convex.fungible` resolves the name directly — the normal way to reach a library; `(@convex.fungible/balance #TOKEN #HOLDER)` calls into it.
- To see the current address: `(*registry*/resolve 'convex.fungible)` as a free query. Addresses are network-specific — resolve on the network in use rather than assuming.

## Register or update — transactions

The registry is actor `#9`, available in code as `*registry*`:

- New name: `(*registry*/create 'my.name #TARGET *address*)` — optional controller, metadata and child arguments follow.
- Change target: `(*registry*/update 'my.name #NEW-TARGET)`
- Change controller: `(*registry*/control 'my.name #NEW-CONTROLLER)`

Creating needs control of the parent namespace: `my.name` requires the `my` node to exist and to trust the caller, otherwise `:TRUST` "Forbidden to create CNS node"; top-level names need special authority. `(*registry*/register {:name …})` is unrelated — it sets metadata on the caller's own account.

## Standard names

`convex.fungible` (fungible tokens) · `convex.trust` (authorisation) · `convex.asset` (generic assets) · `asset.nft.simple` (NFTs) · `asset.multi-token` (multi-token standard).
